findings.text: The condition calls Error(t, ...) and EqualError(t, ...), and both report their own failure on t. When the panic error message differs, for example panic(errors.New("a")) checked against "b", the test gets an extra EqualError failure and then a second one from the Fail on line 25. When the panic value is not an error, only the Fail on line 25 fires. Failures are reported twice, which is noisy and can mislead. The check should compare the message directly, for example panicErr.Error() == errString, without calling the asserting helpers.
